newsitem.title: INDIA: India Andhra Pradesh state shows record rice sale.
newsitem.headline: India Andhra Pradesh state shows record rice sale.

text.p: State-owned Food Corporation of India (FCI) has purchased a record 4.17 million tonnes of rice from the southern state of Andhra Pradesh in the year to September 1997, state officials said on Monday.

They said they were hopeful this procurement figure would rise by another one million tonnes at the request of state chief minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, who has urged the FCI to buy more in view of a bumper crop this year.
Purchases from states across India for FCI's 1996/97 (October-September) procurement year are normally made upto June because that's the time the crop is available in the market.
Officials from the state's Civil Supplies Department said the FCI purchased 3.67 million tonnes in 1995/96, 4.01 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 3.97 million tonnes in 1993/94.
Andhra Pradesh is India's third largest state producer of rice, after West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh.
Civil Supplies Commissioner, H.S. Brahma said that paddy production during the 1996/97 (June-May) crop year was a record 9.9 million tones, up from 9.0 million tonnes in 1995/96.
